import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD in Å²

# Convert steps to time (timestep = 0.001 ps)
time = steps * 0.001  # time in ps

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print("MSD plot saved as msd_plot.png")

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need the linear regime
# Typically, we skip the initial ballistic regime and use the later part
# Let's use the last 80% of the data for fitting
start_idx = int(0.2 * len(time))
time_fit = time[start_idx:]
msd_fit = msd_total[start_idx:]

# Linear fit: MSD = 6*D*t (in 3D)
# So slope = 6*D
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6
# Units: slope is in Ų/ps, so D is in Ų/ps
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Ų = 1e-20 m²
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So 1 Ų/ps = 1e-20 / 1e-12 = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\n=== Diffusion Coefficient Analysis ===")
print(f"Linear fit range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps")
print(f"Number of data points used: {len(time_fit)}")
print(f"Slope of MSD vs time: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"R² value: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6e}")
print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer (in m²/s): {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot with fitted line
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot_with_fit.png', dpi=150)
print("\nMSD plot with fit saved as msd_plot_with_fit.png")

# Save the result to a file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"\nLinear fit statistics:\n")
    f.write(f"Slope = {slope:.6f} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R² = {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"Fit range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps\n")

print("\nResults saved to diffusion_coefficient.txt")

- Read the MSD data
- Fit the linear regime of MSD vs time
- Calculate the diffusion coefficient

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD in Å²

# Convert steps to time (timestep = 0.001 ps)
time = steps * 0.001  # time in ps

# Plot MSD vs time to visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print("MSD plot saved as msd_plot.png")

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need the linear regime
# Typically, we skip the initial ballistic regime and use the later part
# Let's use the last 80% of the data for fitting
start_idx = int(0.2 * len(time))
time_fit = time[start_idx:]
msd_fit = msd_total[start_idx:]

# Linear fit: MSD = 6*D*t (in 3D)
# So slope = 6*D
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6
# Units: slope is in Ų/ps, so D is in Ų/ps
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Ų = 1e-20 m²
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So 1 Ų/ps = 1e-20 / 1e-12 = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\n=== Diffusion Coefficient Analysis ===")
print(f"Linear fit range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps")
print(f"Number of data points used: {len(time_fit)}")
print(f"Slope of MSD vs time: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"R² value: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6e}")
print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer (in m²/s): {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot with fitted line
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.5, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot_with_fit.png', dpi=150)
print("\nMSD plot with fit saved as msd_plot_with_fit.png")

# Save the result to a file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"\nLinear fit statistics:\n")
    f.write(f"Slope = {slope:.6f} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R² = {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"Fit range: {time_fit[0]:.2f} - {time_fit[-1]:.2f} ps\n")

print("\nResults saved to diffusion_coefficient.txt")
"}</action_input>

# LAMMPS input script for melting silicon and computing diffusion coefficient
# Units: metal (eV, Angstrom, ps, K)

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data       si_structure.data
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Set mass (for Si)
mass            1 28.0855

# Neighbor settings
neighbor        2.0 bin
neigh_modify    every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Timestep
timestep        0.001  # 1 fs in metal units

# Thermodynamic output
thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Stage 1: Initial equilibration at 300K (NPT)
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix             1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             10000  # 10 ps equilibration
unfix           1

# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# Time needed: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1000000 steps
fix             2 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             1000000  # 1000 ps heating
unfix           2

# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps
fix             3 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             500000  # 500 ps equilibration
unfix           3

# Stage 4: Production run at 2500K with MSD calculation
# Reset timestep for MSD calculation
reset_timestep  0

# Compute MSD for all atoms
compute         msd_all all msd com yes

# Output MSD data
fix             4 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
fix             msd_output all print 1000 "${step} $(c_msd_all[1]) $(c_msd_all[2]) $(c_msd_all[3]) $(c_msd_all[4])" &
                file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol c_msd_all[4]

# Run for 500 ps to collect MSD data
run             500000

unfix           4
unfix           msd_output

# Calculate self-diffusion coefficient at 2500K

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data       silicon.data
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Set masses (Si atomic mass)
mass            1 28.0855

# Define groups
group           all type 1

# Neighbor list settings
neighbor        2.0 bin
neigh_modify    every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Timestep
timestep        0.001  # 1 fs in metal units

# Thermodynamic output
thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# ============================================
# Stage 1: Initial equilibration at 300K (NPT)
# ============================================
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix             1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             10000  # 10 ps initial equilibration
unfix           1

# ============================================
# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K (NPT)
# Rate: 2.2 K/ps, Time: 1000 ps
# ============================================
fix             2 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             1000000  # 1000 ps heating
unfix           2

# ============================================
# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K (NPT)
# Time: 500 ps with MSD computation
# ============================================

# Reset MSD computation
reset_timestep  0

# Compute MSD
compute         msd all msd com yes

# Output MSD data
fix             3 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
fix             msd_output all print 1000 "${step} $(c_msd[1]) $(c_msd[2]) $(c_msd[3]) $(c_msd[4])" file msd.dat screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

run             500000  # 500 ps equilibration with MSD tracking

unfix           3
unfix           msd_output

Great! The simulation completed successfully. Now I need to extract the MSD data from the log file. The MSD data should be in the third run (stage 3 - equilibration at 2500K). Let me extract that data and calculate the diffusion coefficient.

The Einstein relation for diffusion coefficient is:
D = lim(t→∞) MSD / (6t)

where MSD is the mean squared displacement and t is time.

In LAMMPS with metal units:
- Time is in picoseconds (ps)
- Distance is in Angstroms (Å)
- So MSD is in Å²

The diffusion coefficient will be in Å²/ps, which needs to be converted to m²/s:
1 Å²/ps = 1e-20 m² / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m²/s
</thought>

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
df = pd.read_csv('msd_data.csv')

# Extract step and total MSD
step = df['Step'].values
msd_total = df['c_msd[4]'].values

# Convert step to time (ps)
# timestep = 0.001 ps
time = step * 0.001  # in ps

print(f"Total data points: {len(time)}")
print(f"Time range: {time[0]:.3f} to {time[-1]:.3f} ps")
print(f"MSD range: {msd_total[0]:.6f} to {msd_total[-1]:.6f} Å²")

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print("\nMSD plot saved as msd_plot.png")

# Use the last 80% of data for linear fit (to ensure equilibration)
fit_start_idx = int(0.2 * len(time))
time_fit = time[fit_start_idx:]
msd_fit = msd_total[fit_start_idx:]

print(f"\nUsing data from {time_fit[0]:.3f} to {time_fit[-1]:.3f} ps for fitting")

# Linear regression: MSD = slope * time + intercept
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"\nLinear fit results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.6f} Ų")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6f}")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient using Einstein relation
# D = MSD / (6t) => D = slope / 6
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0  # in Ų/ps

# Convert to m²/s
# 1 Å = 1e-10 m
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# 1 Ų/ps = 1e-20 m² / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

# Plot with fit line
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r--', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit (R² = {r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot_with_fit.png', dpi=150)
print("\nMSD plot with fit saved as msd_plot_with_fit.png")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient of liquid silicon at 2500K\n")
    f.write(f"="*50 + "\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"\nLinear fit details:\n")
    f.write(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Ų/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"Data used: {time_fit[0]:.1f} - {time_fit[-1]:.1f} ps\n")

print("\nResults saved to diffusion_coefficient.txt")
print(f"\n{'='*50}")
print(f"FINAL RESULT: D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")
print(f"{'='*50}")
"}</action_input>

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting and diffusion coefficient calculation
# Units: metal (Angstroms, eV, ps, etc.)
# Atom style: full

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data       si_structure.data
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential (Stillinger-Weber)
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Set neighbor list parameters
neighbor        2.0 bin
neigh_modify    every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Define compute for MSD (will be used during equilibration)
compute         msd all msd com yes

# Initialize velocities at 300K
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian

# Setup thermo output
thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol c_msd[4]

# Heating phase: 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# Temperature change: 2200K, Rate: 2.2 K/ps, Time: 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
timestep        0.001
fix             heat all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)
run             1000000
unfix           heat

# Reset MSD compute before equilibration
uncompute       msd
compute         msd all msd com yes

# Equilibration phase at 2500K for 500 ps = 500,000 steps
fix             equil all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)
run             500000
unfix           equil

# Write final configuration
write_data      final_structure.data

print           "Simulation completed successfully"

print(f"Time range: {time[0]:.3f} to {time[-1]:.3f} ps")
print(f"MSD range: {msd_total[0]:.6f} to {msd_total[-1]:.6f} Å²")

plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print("\nMSD plot saved as msd_plot.png")

# Use the last 80% of data for linear fit (to ensure equilibration)
fit_start_idx = int(0.2 * len(time))

msd_fit = msd_total[fit_start_idx:]

print(f"\nUsing data from {time_fit[0]:.3f} to {time_fit[-1]:.3f} ps for fitting")

# Linear regression: MSD = slope * time + intercept
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")

D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6f} Ų/ps")
print(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s")

plt.ylabel('MSD (Ų)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time at 2500K', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot_with_fit.png', dpi=150)
print("\nMSD plot with fit saved as msd_plot_with_fit.png")

    f.write(f"D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")

It transforms the primitive structure returned by the database into its conventional crystallographic form using symmetry operations, and exports the result in CIF format to a specified file path. This tool is valuable for workflows that require standardized crystal structure representations — such as simulations, visualization, structure matching, or publication. It avoids the need for manual structure transformation or dealing with primitive cells when conventional representation is needed.

How this tool works:

Tool: convert_structure_to_lammps_data
Description: Converts a CIF-format structure file into a LAMMPS data file using a specified atom style.

This tool converts a crystal structure provided in CIF format (as a file) into a LAMMPS-compatible data file. Internally, it reads the CIF structure file using pymatgen, transforms it into a Structure object, and then serializes it to a LAMMPS data format using the LammpsData class. It supports configurable atom styles such as "atomic" or "charge", allowing flexibility based on simulation requirements.
This enables seamless transformation of standardized crystallographic data into simulation-ready LAMMPS input files, streamlining the setup process for molecular dynamics workflows.

When to use: When to use this tool:
    - Use when you need to convert crystallographic structure data in CIF format into a LAMMPS-compatible `.data` file.
    - Best suited for setting up molecular dynamics simulations where LAMMPS is the engine, and structure data is sourced from databases like Materials Project or experimental CIFs.
    - Avoid when your structure data is already in LAMMPS format or requires extensive pre-processing (e.g., force field assignments).
    - Recommended for automating simulation pipelines that begin with standardized structural data and end in LAMMPS-ready input formats.

How this tool works:
    - The tool reads the `.cif` file using `pymatgen.core.Structure.from_file` to create a Structure object.
    - The `LammpsData.from_structure` function is called, using the chosen `atom_style` to format the atomic data accordingly.
    - The resulting LAMMPS data file is written to the path specified by `output_file`.
    - The tool does not apply force fields or assign charges explicitly; it assumes the structure is already complete and appropriate for the selected `atom_style`.

    1.  Ensure you have a valid CIF file containing the crystallographic structure of the material you want to simulate. Use the tool `get_structure_from_mp_text` to obtain one.

- output_file (str, required): Path where the LAMMPS data file will be saved.
This is the destination file path where the generated LAMMPS-compatible data file will be written. The output file will contain the atomic positions, types, and other necessary information formatted for LAMMPS simulations.
- atom_style (str, optional, default: charge): Atom style to be used in the LAMMPS data file, defaults to "charge".
Specifies the LAMMPS atom style to use when formatting the data file. Common values include: - "atomic": Includes atomic positions and mass, no charges. - "charge": Includes atomic charges in addition to position and mass. The choice of style should match the `atom_style` directive in the LAMMPS input script. Defaults to "charge" if nothing provided. This tool takes the path to an image file containing a plot and a natural-language query about that plot. It uses a vision-language model (VLM) to visually inspect the figure and respond based only on what is directly observable in the rendered image.
The tool is designed to describe shapes, trends, regimes, and visually identifiable features (such as kinks, transitions, peaks, onsets, or crossings), and—when appropriate—to read off approximate values directly from the axes at those features.
Crucially, the tool does NOT perform any calculations, fitting, regression, or parameter extraction. If the query requires a computed or inferred quantity rather than a directly readable or visually observable feature, the tool will refuse and state that it can only provide visual descriptions and directly readable values. Because the tool relies on a vision-language model and a rendered image, its answers are inherently approximate, potentially noisy, and may sometimes be incorrect or incomplete. The quality and reliability of the response depend strongly on image resolution, plot clarity, axis labeling, marker density, and overall figure design. Users should treat the output as a qualitative, assistive interpretation and should validate important conclusions using proper quantitative analysis tools or the underlying data.

When to use: When to use this tool:

    - Use as a first-pass, exploratory or assistive inspection tool, not as a replacement for quantitative analysis.

How this tool works:
    - The image at the given path is loaded and analyzed by a vision-language model (VLM).
    - The model performs visual inspection only: it looks at shapes, trends, patterns, and visibly identifiable features in the figure.
    - The model may report approximate values only when they can be directly read from the axes at a clearly visible feature (e.g., a labeled tick near a visible transition).
    - The model does not have access to the underlying data and does not perform any numerical computation, fitting, or measurement.
    - Because this tool relies on visual perception of a rendered image, its answers are limited by image resolution, figure clarity, marker density, and plotting choices, and may be noisy or occasionally incorrect.

    3.  Validate any important conclusions using the underlying data or dedicated analysis tools. If the answer is unclear or unreliable, consider replotting (e.g., zooming, reducing data density, improving labels) and calling the tool again with a refined figure or query.

This parameter specifies the absolute or relative path to an image file (e.g., PNG, JPG) that contains a plot or figure. The image should be readable by the backend and should include visible axes, labels, and plotted data so that visual features and directly readable values can be identified.

# Units: metal (eV, Angstroms, ps, etc.)

# Initialization
units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data si_structure.data
replicate 3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style sw
pair_coeff * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Define groups
group all type 1

# Neighbor settings
neighbor 2.0 bin
neigh_modify every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Timestep
timestep 0.001  # 1 fs

# Thermodynamic output
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# ========================================
# Stage 1: Initial minimization
# ========================================
min_style cg
minimize 1.0e-6 1.0e-8 10000 100000

# Reset timestep
reset_timestep 0

# ========================================
# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# ========================================
# Temperature change: 2200 K
# Rate: 2.2 K/ps
# Time needed: 2200/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps

velocity all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix npt_heat all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)

run 1000000

unfix npt_heat
reset_timestep 0

# ========================================
# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps
# ========================================
# 500 ps = 500,000 steps

fix npt_equil all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)

run 500000

unfix npt_equil
reset_timestep 0

# ========================================
# Stage 4: Production run with MSD calculation
# ========================================
# Run for 500 ps to collect MSD data
# 500 ps = 500,000 steps

# Compute MSD
compute msd_compute all msd com yes

# Output MSD data
fix msd_output all print 100 "$(step) $(c_msd_compute[1]) $(c_msd_compute[2]) $(c_msd_compute[3]) $(c_msd_compute[4])" file msd_data.txt screen no title "# step msd_x msd_y msd_z msd_total"

fix npt_prod all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)

run 500000

unfix npt_prod
unfix msd_output

print "Simulation completed successfully"
"}</action_input>

Good! The MSD data file exists. Now I'll create a Python script to:
1. Read the MSD data
2. Calculate the diffusion coefficient from the linear fit of MSD vs time
3. Convert to m²/s units

In LAMMPS metal units:
- Time is in ps
- Distance is in Angstroms
- MSD is in Angstroms²

The Einstein relation: D = lim(t→∞) MSD/(6t)
Or from the slope of MSD vs time: D = slope/6

To convert from Angstroms²/ps to m²/s:
- 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m
- 1 ps = 1e-12 s
- 1 Angstrom²/ps = 1e-20 m² / 1e-12 s = 1e-8 m²/s
</thought>

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt', comments='#')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD

# Convert steps to time (ps)
# timestep = 0.001 ps
dt = 0.001  # ps
time = steps * dt

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1)
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time', fontsize=14)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# Use the linear regime for fitting
# Typically, we skip the initial part and use the middle-to-late portion
# Let's use data from 50 ps onwards to ensure we're in the diffusive regime
start_time = 50.0  # ps
start_idx = np.searchsorted(time, start_time)

# Fit linear regression to the linear regime
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time[start_idx:], msd_total[start_idx:])

print(f"Linear fit from {start_time} ps onwards:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom²/ps")
print(f"R²: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Standard error: {std_err:.6e}")

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6 (Einstein relation in 3D)
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient (Angstrom²/ps): {D_angstrom_ps:.6e}")

# 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# 1 Angstrom²/ps = 1e-8 m²/s
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"Diffusion coefficient (m²/s): {D_m2_s:.6e}")

# Save result
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_m2_s:.6e} m²/s\n")
    f.write(f"Slope of MSD vs time: {slope:.6f} Angstrom²/ps\n")
    f.write(f"R² value: {r_value**2:.6f}\n")
    f.write(f"Fit range: {start_time} ps to {time[-1]:.1f} ps\n")

# Create a plot with the fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time[start_idx:], slope * time[start_idx:] + intercept, 'r--', linewidth=2, label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)', fontsize=12)
plt.title(f'MSD vs Time with Linear Fit\nD = {D_m2_s:.3e} m²/s', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.savefig('msd_with_fit.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

print(f"\nPlots saved: msd_plot.png and msd_with_fit.png")
print(f"Results saved: diffusion_coefficient.txt")
"}</action_input>

# LAMMPS input script for melting silicon and computing diffusion coefficient
# Units: metal (eV, Angstrom, ps, K)

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure and replicate
read_data       si_structure.data
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Set mass (for Si)
mass            1 28.0855

# Neighbor settings
neighbor        2.0 bin
neigh_modify    every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Timestep
timestep        0.001  # 1 fs in metal units

# Thermodynamic output
thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol

# Stage 1: Initial equilibration at 300K (NPT)
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian
fix             1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             10000  # 10 ps equilibration
unfix           1

# Stage 2: Heating from 300K to 2500K at 2.2 K/ps
# Time needed: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps = 1000000 steps
fix             2 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             1000000  # 1000 ps heating
unfix           2

# Stage 3: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps
fix             3 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
run             500000  # 500 ps equilibration
unfix           3

# Stage 4: Production run at 2500K with MSD calculation
# Reset timestep for MSD calculation
reset_timestep  0

# Compute MSD for all atoms
compute         msd_all all msd com yes

# Output MSD data
fix             4 all npt temp 2500.0 2500.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
fix             msd_output all print 1000 "${step} $(c_msd_all[1]) $(c_msd_all[2]) $(c_msd_all[3]) $(c_msd_all[4])" &
                file msd_data.txt screen no title "# Step MSD_x MSD_y MSD_z MSD_total"

thermo          1000
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol c_msd_all[4]

# Run for 500 ps to collect MSD data
run             500000

unfix           4
unfix           msd_output

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd.dat', skiprows=2)

# Extract time and MSD
# Column 0: timestep
# Column 4: total MSD (c_msd[4])
timesteps = data[:, 0]
msd = data[:, 4]

# Convert timesteps to time in picoseconds
# timestep = 0.001 ps, output every 100 timesteps
time_ps = timesteps * 0.001  # in picoseconds

# For diffusion coefficient calculation, we need to fit the linear region
# Typically, we skip the initial part and use the later linear region
# Let's use data from 100 ps to 500 ps (avoiding initial transient)
start_time = 100  # ps
end_time = 500    # ps

# Find indices for the fitting range
start_idx = np.argmin(np.abs(time_ps - start_time))
end_idx = np.argmin(np.abs(time_ps - end_time))

# Extract data for fitting
time_fit = time_ps[start_idx:end_idx]
msd_fit = msd[start_idx:end_idx]

# Linear regression: MSD = 6*D*t
# So slope = 6*D
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6
D_A2_ps = slope / 6.0  # in Angstrom^2/ps

# Convert to m^2/s
# 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m
# 1 ps = 1e-12 s
# So 1 A^2/ps = (1e-10)^2 / 1e-12 = 1e-8 m^2/s
D_m2_s = D_A2_ps * 1e-8

print(f"Fitting range: {start_time} ps to {end_time} ps")
print(f"Number of data points used: {len(time_fit)}")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"R^2 value: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_A2_ps:.6e} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"Diffusion coefficient: {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Plot MSD vs time
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_ps, msd, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')
plt.plot(time_fit, msd_fit, 'r-', linewidth=2, label=f'Fit region ({start_time}-{end_time} ps)')
plt.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'g--', linewidth=2, label=f'Linear fit (R²={r_value**2:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Time (ps)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('MSD (Angstrom²)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_plot.png', dpi=150)
print("\nPlot saved as msd_plot.png")
"

# LAMMPS input script for silicon melting simulation
# Task: Calculate self-diffusion coefficient at 2500K

# Initialization
units           metal
atom_style      full
boundary        p p p

# Read structure
read_data       silicon.data

# Replicate 3x3x3
replicate       3 3 3

# Define potential - Stillinger-Weber
pair_style      sw
pair_coeff      * * /potentials/SW/Si.sw Si

# Settings
neighbor        0.3 bin
neigh_modify    every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Initialize velocities at 300K
velocity        all create 300.0 12345 dist gaussian

# Define computes for output
compute         myTemp all temp
compute         myPress all pressure myTemp

# Thermodynamic output
thermo_style    custom step temp press density pe ke etotal vol
thermo          1000

# ============================================
# Stage 1: Heating from 300K to 2500K
# Heating rate: 2.2 K/ps
# Time needed: (2500-300)/2.2 = 1000 ps
# Timestep: 0.001 ps = 1 fs
# Steps: 1,000,000
# ============================================

timestep        0.001

fix             1 all npt temp 300.0 2500.0 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)

run             1000000

unfix           1

# ============================================
# Stage 2: Equilibration at 2500K for 500 ps
# Steps: 500,000
# ============================================

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Calculate diffusion coefficient from LAMMPS MSD data using Einstein relation.
"""

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Read MSD data
data = np.loadtxt('msd_data.txt')
steps = data[:, 0]
msd_total = data[:, 4]  # Total MSD (x+y+z)

# Convert steps to time (timestep = 0.001 ps)
dt = 0.001  # ps
time = steps * dt  # ps

# Use the linear region for fitting (typically after initial transient)
# Skip first 10% of data to avoid initial transient
skip = len(time) // 10
time_fit = time[skip:]
msd_fit = msd_total[skip:]

# Linear regression: MSD = 6*D*t
# slope = 6*D
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(time_fit, msd_fit)

# Calculate diffusion coefficient
# D = slope / 6
# Units: MSD is in Angstrom^2, time is in ps
# D is in Angstrom^2/ps
D_angstrom_ps = slope / 6.0

# Convert to m^2/s
# 1 Angstrom = 10^-10 m
# 1 ps = 10^-12 s
# D[m^2/s] = D[Angstrom^2/ps] * (10^-10 m)^2 / (10^-12 s)
#          = D[Angstrom^2/ps] * 10^-20 / 10^-12
#          = D[Angstrom^2/ps] * 10^-8
D_m2_s = D_angstrom_ps * 1e-8

print(f"\n=== Diffusion Coefficient Calculation ===")
print(f"Linear fit parameters:")
print(f"  Slope: {slope:.6e} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"  Intercept: {intercept:.6e} Angstrom^2")
print(f"  R^2: {r_value**2:.6f}")
print(f"  Std error: {std_err:.6e}")
print(f"\nDiffusion coefficient:")
print(f"  D = {D_angstrom_ps:.6e} Angstrom^2/ps")
print(f"  D = {D_m2_s:.6e} m^2/s")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {D_m2_s:.2e}")

# Save result to file
with open('diffusion_coefficient.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"{D_m2_s:.6e}\n")

# Create plots
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))

# Plot 1: Full MSD vs time
ax1.plot(time, msd_total, 'b-', linewidth=1, label='MSD data')
ax1.set_xlabel('Time (ps)')
ax1.set_ylabel('MSD (Angstrom^2)')
ax1.set_title('Mean Squared Displacement vs Time')
ax1.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
ax1.legend()

# Plot 2: Linear fit region
ax2.plot(time_fit, msd_fit, 'b.', markersize=2, label='MSD data (fit region)', alpha=0.5)
ax2.plot(time_fit, slope * time_fit + intercept, 'r-', linewidth=2, 
         label=f'Linear fit: slope={slope:.2e}\nR²={r_value**2:.4f}')
ax2.set_xlabel('Time (ps)')
ax2.set_ylabel('MSD (Angstrom^2)')
ax2.set_title('Linear Regression for Diffusion Coefficient')
ax2.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
ax2.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('msd_analysis.png', dpi=150)
print(f"\nPlot saved as msd_analysis.png")

print(f"\n=== Analysis Complete ===")
